title.es: Simulación: la jornada abierta del barrio

es: Resolver una simulación de jornada abierta integrando relato breve, concesión con tacto, contingencias y un plan con plazo, y reparar el propio texto antes de entregarlo.

teaching.en: I would like to put forward a proposal for the open day: a story workshop in the square, run by volunteers.
teaching.es: Me gustaría presentar una propuesta para la jornada abierta: un taller de relatos en la plaza, a cargo de voluntarios.
teaching.explanationEs: Put forward a proposal ofrece la idea sin imponerla; es la apertura con tacto.
segments: I would like to put forward a proposal for the open
day: a story workshop in the square, run by volunteers.
teaching.audioText: I would like to put forward a proposal for the open day: a story workshop in the square, run by volunteers.

teaching.en: By last spring, the square had been empty for months, so a stall of stories could now rally support for bringing neighbours back.
teaching.es: Hacia la primavera pasada, la plaza llevaba meses vacía, así que un puesto de relatos podía ahora ganar apoyos para traer de vuelta a los vecinos.
teaching.explanationEs: Un contexto breve en pasado: lo anterior al momento del relato lleva had + participio.

stall of stories could now rally support for bringing neighbours back.

teaching.en: Anyone may raise an objection, and a good speaker will concede a fair point, then reach a compromise.
teaching.es: Cualquiera puede plantear una objeción, y quien habla bien concede una observación justa y después llega a un acuerdo.
teaching.explanationEs: Conceder no cambia la postura: prepara el terreno para el acuerdo.

teaching.en: Much as I appreciate the concern, I was wondering whether the volunteers could take on board a little extra work.
teaching.es: Aunque agradezco la preocupación, me preguntaba si los voluntarios podrían asumir un poco más de trabajo.
teaching.explanationEs: Much as reconoce la objeción sin but; la pregunta indirecta con whether mantiene el orden afirmativo.

teaching.en: Should it rain, the workshop will move into the hall, so a tight budget need not spoil the day.
teaching.es: Si lloviera, el taller se trasladará al salón, así que un presupuesto ajustado no tiene por qué arruinar el día.
teaching.explanationEs: Should + sujeto + verbo base: contingencia formal, sin if y sin -s en el verbo.

teaching.explanationEs: By = para esa fecha o antes; will have + participio marca lo ya cumplido en ese momento.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase abre tu propuesta con más tacto ante el vecindario?

choices.text: You must accept my idea for the open day, because it is better.
My idea is the only one that can work for the open day.
I would like to put forward a proposal for the open day.

feedback.es: Una propuesta se ofrece, no se impone: I would like to put forward abre la intervención con tacto ante un público que duda.

hint.es: Una propuesta se ofrece, no se impone.

origin.text: You are speaking at the neighbourhood meeting. The budget is small, and two neighbours already look doubtful.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si lloviera, todo se trasladará al salón y nadie tendrá que cancelar.»

feedback.es: Should + sujeto + verbo base sustituye a if en una contingencia formal: Should it rain.

hint.es: Tras should invertido el verbo va en forma base.

origin.text: The workshop is outdoors, so the organisers have a plan for bad weather: Should it ___, everything will move into the hall, and nobody will need to cancel.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Para el viernes habremos confirmado el puesto.»

answer.text: By Friday, we will have confirmed the stall
accepted: By Friday, we will have confirmed the stall
We will have confirmed the stall by Friday

feedback.es: By marca el plazo y will have + participio presenta la tarea como cumplida para entonces.

hint.es: Empieza por el plazo; después va el futuro con will have.

prompt.es: Responde a esta objeción de Carlos con concesión y tacto.

choices.text: Much as I appreciate the concern, I was wondering whether volunteers could help.
Much as I appreciate the concern, but volunteers could help us with that.
I understand your worry, yet you are wrong about the noise and the budget.

feedback.es: Reconoce la objeción con much as y pide ayuda con una pregunta indirecta; la variante con but añade un conector sobrante y la que empieza por I understand niega la objeción sin tacto.

origin.text: Carlos: The budget is tight, and a workshop in the square will bring noise. Besides, nobody has promised to run the stall.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué prevé la oradora si llueve el día de la jornada.

choices.text: The stall will be cancelled for the day.
The workshop will be held in the hall.
The council will postpone the event until Friday.

feedback.es: La oradora usa Should it rain, we will move into the hall: el taller se traslada al salón; el viernes es el plazo para confirmarlo todo.

origin.audio: By last spring the square had been empty for months. Now, I would like to put forward a proposal: a story workshop, run by volunteers, with a small stall for books. Should it rain, we will move into the hall, and by Friday we will have confirmed everything with the council.

prompt.es: Escucha a la presidenta y elige qué valoró más de la intervención de Sara.

choices.text: That she persuaded Carlos to drop every objection about the budget.
That she solved the money problem by finding extra funds.
That her tactful wording turned an objection into a shared plan.
That she kept the discussion short by ignoring the objection.

feedback.es: La presidenta destaca la formulación: una pregunta indirecta convirtió la objeción en un plan; no dice que Carlos renunciara a todo ni que apareciera dinero nuevo.

origin.audio: Later that evening, the chair of the residents' association described the meeting to a friend. Sara's proposal, she said, had won the room over: a story workshop in the square, run by volunteers. Carlos had raised the budget, which was a fair point, and Sara had answered without any sign of anger. What impressed the chair most was the wording. Instead of insisting, Sara asked whether the volunteers could bring the materials, and that small question turned an objection into a plan. By the end, nobody was arguing about the money. They were arguing about who would bring the chairs.

prompt.es: Localiza el error del cartel: ¿de qué categoría es y cuál es la regla?

choices.text: Register: the clause after because needs a noun instead.
Narrative style: the past perfect is not needed, so had been should be was.
Tact: the request should become an indirect question.
Contingency: after should, the verb stays in base form.

feedback.es: Should the weather gets rompe la regla de la contingencia formal: tras should invertido el verbo va en forma base (get). Las demás frases del cartel son correctas.

origin.text: Notice for residents. The open day will begin at ten in the square. Should the weather gets bad, the workshop will take place in the hall. We kindly ask volunteers to arrive by nine, because the stall must be ready before the first visitors come. By last spring, the square had been empty for months, so every helping hand will be welcome.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si queremos cumplir el plazo, los carteles deben imprimirse para el viernes.»

feedback.es: Meet the deadline es la colocación habitual para cumplir un plazo; by Friday y by Thursday marcan las fechas límite.

origin.text: The organisers are working on a tight budget. If we want to ___ the deadline, the posters must be printed by Friday.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención (180–320 palabras): idea, contexto, objeción, plan, plazo.

answer.text: I would like to put forward a proposal for the open day: a story workshop in the square. By last spring, the square had been empty for months, and many neighbours told me they missed a place to meet. A workshop with a small book stall could change that. The square belongs to all of us, and a story is the cheapest way to fill it. I know that a new idea always raises questions, and I welcome them, because a fair point can only improve the plan. I understand that the budget is tight, and much as I appreciate your concern, I believe we can manage. I was wondering whether the volunteers could bring the books and the chairs, so the cost would be almost nothing, and nobody would need to spend money on anything else. Should it rain, we will move the workshop into the hall. Failing that, we can shorten the morning. If everyone agrees, I will confirm the stall by Friday, and by Saturday we will have prepared the posters. Shall we agree on that? Thank you for listening, and I hope you will join us.
accepted: I would like to put forward a proposal for the open day: a story workshop in the square. By last spring, the square had been empty for months, and many neighbours told me they missed a place to meet. A workshop with a small book stall could change that. The square belongs to all of us, and a story is the cheapest way to fill it. I know that a new idea always raises questions, and I welcome them, because a fair point can only improve the plan. I understand that the budget is tight, and much as I appreciate your concern, I believe we can manage. I was wondering whether the volunteers could bring the books and the chairs, so the cost would be almost nothing, and nobody would need to spend money on anything else. Should it rain, we will move the workshop into the hall. Failing that, we can shorten the morning. If everyone agrees, I will confirm the stall by Friday, and by Saturday we will have prepared the posters. Shall we agree on that? Thank you for listening, and I hope you will join us.

Let me put forward a proposal: a story workshop for the open day. When I was a child, the square used to be full of people, and I would love to see that again. Stories can bring neighbours together, and a simple workshop is a good way to start. I also believe that a workshop like this costs very little and gives a lot back. Nobody needs a big stage to tell a story, only a few chairs and a little time. Fair enough, the budget is limited. Much as I would like a bigger stall, I am sure the volunteers can help, and I was wondering whether the library could lend us some books for the morning. In the event of rain, the workshop will take place in the hall. By Friday I will have confirmed the stall with the council, and the posters will be ready by Saturday. That is our deadline, and I am confident that we can meet it together. Are we all happy with this plan? Thank you for listening, and I hope that many of you will come and tell a story of your own.

I would like to propose a workshop where neighbours write a short story together, one sentence each. The idea came from last year, when a stranger left a notebook on a bench and within a week the whole street had filled it. I understand that some of you worry about the noise and the cost, and I accept that both are fair points. Much as I am keen on the idea, I would not want it to divide us. I was wondering whether we could try it for one morning, with a small stall and a handful of volunteers, and then decide. Should the weather turn bad, we can use the library. By Friday I will have spoken to the volunteers, and by the following Friday we will have a clear answer. If the morning goes badly, at least we will have tried. I am not asking for a big budget, only for one morning and a little goodwill from all of us. Does that seem a fair compromise? Thank you for listening, and please tell me what you think before we vote.

feedback.es: Una intervención completa propone con tacto, da contexto, responde a la objeción, prevé imprevistos y fija un plazo.

origin.text: Jornada abierta del barrio. Presenta tu idea, cuenta brevemente por qué la propones, responde con tacto a la objeción de que el presupuesto es ajustado y cierra con un plan, una contingencia y un plazo (el viernes).

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender el cartel sobre cómo ven las organizadoras a los vecinos?

choices.text: They see the neighbours as writers of the story, not just an audience.
They want the neighbours to bring their own supplies to save money.
They are embarrassed about how empty the square has looked.
They fear that the neighbours will laugh at the poster.

feedback.es: La página vacía es una metáfora y la nota pequeña invita a aportar el propio final: los vecinos son coautores; la pluma es una imagen, no un coste.

origin.text: The organisers hung a poster on the library door. It reads: Our square is an empty page. Come and write a story with us. Below it, in smaller letters, somebody has added: Bring your own pen, and your own ending. Several neighbours stopped to read it, and two of them laughed.
